observationsNotFindings: The strongest feature of this draft is that its edit is specified as operands rather than as description. The before-operand is a literal fenced string that occurs exactly once in the live file with no backslash bytes, the after-operand differs from it by seven character-level edits I could enumerate exhaustively, and the inserted row is a literal markdown line whose cells I could compare to the frozen candidate one at a time. An apply step has nothing left to interpret, and a reviewer has nothing left to take on trust.

The one deliberate divergence from the frozen candidate is the harness cell citing D-169, and the draft anticipates the objection rather than hoping it passes: it states the reason — the candidate assigned no number and therefore omitted it — and asserts that all other cells match at the JSON-value level. I tested that assertion constructively and it holds exactly. A divergence that is disclosed, explained and bounded is not the same defect as a divergence that is merely present.

Several arithmetic claims could have been carried over from a snapshot and quietly gone stale, since D-167 and D-168 both landed recently. Each one I could check is true against live bytes: condition 2 at 4 of 32, D-167's cardinality-27 provenance, D-168's zero cardinality effect, the 65-row preamble, 31 gate rows with DR-G31 last, and 28 OPEN with 3 HARD-BLOCKED. The HARD-BLOCKED figure is worth a note: the live table has two cells reading exactly HARD-BLOCKED and one reading 'HARD-BLOCKED pending selector refresh', and the live condition-4 cell itself counts those as 3, so the draft's figure follows the register's own convention rather than inventing one.

The entry is a naming act that repeatedly declines to be an eligibility act. It names a gate, moves the naming half of condition 4, and then states in item 6 that gates 2 and 3 still do not hold, gate 1 Class A is not opened, gates 4 and 5 are not performed, and DR-114 stays OPEN. The temptation in a three-limb act is to let the naming carry an implication about readiness; this one closes that door explicitly.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No MUST-FIX, no SHOULD-FIX. 20 attacks run, 20 refuted. The decisive checks are the ones an apply step would execute, and the draft specifies its edit as operands rather than description, so all of them are mechanical. The condition-4 before-operand occurs exactly once in live file 08 and contains no backslash bytes; the after-operand occurs zero times, so the edit has not already been applied; and diffing the two shows exactly seven character-level changes, every one intended — owners 31 to 32, required names 27 to 28, ' / D-169' into the decision list, '; G32 named under D-169', and OPEN 28 to 29, with HARD-BLOCKED correctly unmoved and every other clause byte-identical. The insertion point is uniquely determined: DR-G31 is the last gate row and '## Blueprint-readiness decision' follows it and occurs once. The inserted row has 8 cells and seven are byte-identical to both the frozen candidate and naming v2; the eighth differs only by inserting 'D-169; ' into the harness cell, which I verified constructively and which the draft discloses and explains, since the candidate could not cite a number it had not been assigned. Its thirteen FC-JOIN tokens are ordered-equal to live actor-join v8. Every cited digest recomputes, including the post-D-167/D-168 file 08 and COORD. Every checkable arithmetic and provenance claim is true on live bytes: condition 2 at 4 of 32, D-167's cardinality-27 provenance, D-168's zero cardinality effect, the exact 65-row preamble, and D-169 as the next unused heading. The entry names a gate while explicitly declining to be an eligibility act — item 6 keeps gates 2 and 3 not holding and DR-114 OPEN. One coverage limit to note: I verified my own Stage A verdict completely, digest and ACCEPT 0/0, but the dispatch forbids reading the other reviewer, so I confirmed only the existence and digest of the Codex Stage A verdict and make no claim about its content. Treat the dual-ACCEPT premise as established by both Stage A verdicts read together, not by mine. This CONSENT is turn 1 of 3 and is the Claude lane's alone.
